positioning.text: SenDISA, an AI engine that fuses video, ANPR, GPS, LiDAR and acoustic data into court-grade evidence and automated workflows for government. Sold as a detection and intelligence layer that runs on cameras a city already owns.

target_customers.text: 27 Smart City customers in North America at FY26 close, reached largely through channel partners rather than a direct field team.
US and Canadian cities: Pittsburgh Parking Authority, Toronto Exhibition Place, Kitchener, Mississauga, Medford, Las Vegas, Calgary and Montreal.

key_capabilities.text: Runs on the city's existing camera estate and VMS rather than a proprietary camera fleet, which removes the day-one hardware bill.
One engine spans parking and curb, road defects (40-plus types with severity ratings), asset and signage cataloguing, and worksite safety from the same patrol pass.
Human-in-the-loop by design: the AI detects and evidences, a trained officer reviews every event and makes every enforcement decision.
Open REST APIs and webhooks into existing ERP, GIS, asset, ticketing, payment and permit systems, with 200-plus technology partners.

pricing_summary.text: No public price list. Sold as an annual subscription with no upfront capital expenditure and multi-year payment plans. Disclosed contract values imply roughly A$1 per head of population per year in large cities: Calgary at A$1.9M in year one and A$4.6M over five years.

recent_changes.text: FY26: ARR reached A$11.7M, up 17%; cash receipts a record A$16.0M; EBITDA A$2.0M, up 23.6%; customer churn 5.6%. Revenue finished only slightly ahead of the prior year as NVIDIA hardware supply issues pushed projects into FY27.

FY26 added five North American city contracts - Pittsburgh Parking Authority, Toronto Exhibition Place, Birmingham, Kitchener and Mississauga - taking the North American Smart City base to 27, with four already live.
FY26 multi-year renewals at Las Vegas, Cairns, Ipswich and Newcastle.
FY25: revenue A$15.4M, up 27%, and a first net profit of about A$450k after a A$3.6M loss in FY24.

review_weaknesses.text: Market capitalisation sits around A$25M in mid-2026, against Genetec's 2,100-plus employees and Arrive's 90-country footprint. Expect vendor-viability questions in any large US procurement.
Churn was 5.6% in FY26, which contradicts the long-running investor narrative of negligible churn.
North American delivery runs largely through channel partners rather than a direct field team, so support reaches the customer through a third party.

quotes.quote: Annualised recurring revenue grew to $11.7 million, up 17% on the prior year, cash receipts reached a record $16.0 million and customer churn was just 5.6%.

Global supply-chain disruptions, particularly around the NVIDIA-based hardware used in many of our deployments, combined with more cautious customer spending, delayed several projects in Singapore and Australia moving some upfront revenue that we had expected in FY26 into FY27.

positioning.text: A unified physical security platform company. Security Center brings video, access control, ALPR, intrusion and communications into one system, and AutoVu is its ALPR module for parking enforcement. Sold exclusively through certified channel partners.

target_customers.text: 42,500 clients across 159 countries, served through a worldwide network of certified channel partners and consultants.
US parking and campus enforcement: City of Fort Lauderdale and Cornell University are among the published AutoVu customers.
Key markets are public safety, government, education, healthcare, retail, banking, energy and transportation. Parking is one application of a broader security platform.

key_capabilities.text: AutoVu mobile and fixed ALPR enforces permits, time limits, pay-by-plate and scofflaw lists in a single patrol pass, using SharpX cameras on enforcement vehicles.
AutoVu Free-Flow tracks occupancy and violations in gateless lots as vehicles enter and exit.
AutoVu Managed Services hosts the ALPR system in the cloud, removing installation and maintenance overhead.
Unified security: body-worn devices, video, access control and intercom in one platform, which keeps operator training low and covers officer safety.
Open architecture with an SDK and partner programmes, positioned explicitly to help customers scale without vendor lock-in.

pricing_summary.text: No public pricing: Genetec sells only through certified channel partners, so price is quoted per project by a reseller. Its strongest published commercial evidence is payback rather than price - Fort Lauderdale recouped its ALPR investment in about two months.

recent_changes.text: Corporate fact sheet dated 15 July 2024 lists 2,100-plus employees worldwide, 42,500 clients and 159 countries, with experience centres including Washington DC.
Company profile data puts headcount at about 2,385 and growing 6.3% year on year, with roughly half in Canada and 9% in the United States.
Security Center SaaS now offers access control and video surveillance as a service alongside the on-premises platform.

review_weaknesses.text: Parking is one module of a security platform, not the product. AutoVu sits inside Security Center, so a parking team buys into a wider security estate and its upgrade cycle.
Channel-only distribution means no direct price, no direct implementation relationship, and partner capability that varies by region.
ALPR runs on Genetec's own SharpX cameras fitted to patrol vehicles rather than the city's existing camera estate, so detection coverage is bounded by the number of vehicles you equip.
No published road-condition, asset-register or kerb-inventory capability, so a city wanting more than enforcement from the same patrol needs a second system.
Only about 9% of staff are based in the United States despite it being a core market, so US delivery leans on the partner network.

hiring_signals.text: About 130 active job postings, weighted to technical (31%) and sales (15%) roles.

quotes.quote: Within the first eight months of installing its first AutoVu ALPR system, the City of Fort Lauderdale was able to boot over 600 scofflaw vehicles and collect over $200,000 in unpaid fines.
Headquartered in Montreal, Canada, Genetec serves its customers via an extensive network of certified channel partners and consultants in over 159 countries.

positioning.text: The demand and payments side of parking, not enforcement. Arrive is EasyPark Group renamed in June 2025, parent of ParkMobile, EasyPark, Flowbird, RingGo, Parkopedia and Yellowbrick, present in 90-plus countries and 20,000 cities.

target_customers.text: ParkMobile is the group's North American brand, available in over 700 US cities for finding, paying for and reserving parking.
Flowbird delivers mobility solutions in over 6,000 cities across 80 countries, including pay stations and transport ticketing.
Cities, operators, fleets and automakers, with in-car integration through Parkopedia.

key_capabilities.text: Digital parking payments at scale through ParkMobile, EasyPark, RingGo and Yellowbrick, owned outright rather than integrated.
Flowbird pay stations, park-and-charge and smart ticketing devices for on-street parking and public transport.
Parkopedia supplies in-dash parking and charging data, in-car payments and GPS-free indoor navigation to automakers.
Mobility data and planning: demand insight, traffic reduction analysis and public transport route and schedule optimisation.

pricing_summary.text: No published municipal pricing. Consumer transaction pricing is public through the apps; city and operator contracts are not disclosed.

recent_changes.text: 12 June 2025: EasyPark Group renamed itself Arrive, becoming the parent brand for EasyPark, Flowbird, ParkMobile, Parkopedia, RingGo, Yellowbrick and YourParkingSpace. The consumer apps keep their own names.
To take the name, EasyPark bought the rights to 'Arrive' from Flash, which had held them since its 2021 merger with the earlier Arrive Mobility (ParkWhiz and BestParking). Terms were not disclosed.
February 2025: completed the acquisition of Parkopedia, adding in-car data and payment technology.
January 2025: completed the acquisition of Flowbird Group, adding pay-and-display machines, software and park-and-charge.
September 2024: Flash and EasyPark subsidiary ParkMobile agreed a strategic partnership sharing parking reservation inventory and infrastructure.

review_weaknesses.text: No published violation-detection or mobile ALPR enforcement product. Arrive sells demand, payments and data, so it does not compete for the enforcement decision at all.
Three major changes are still bedding in - Flowbird acquired January 2025, Parkopedia February 2025, group rebrand June 2025 - which is a lot of change for a city signing a multi-year contract.
The brand is new and shares a name with a different, older US parking company: Flash still operates the former Arrive Mobility assets, ParkWhiz and BestParking. Expect confusion in US procurement.

quotes.quote: The consumer brands and mobile apps, such as EasyPark, RingGo, ParkMobile, and Flowbird, will remain unaffected for the foreseeable future. Arrive will act as the predominant corporate body to the consumer brands.
ParkMobile, LLC, is the leading provider of smart parking and mobility solutions in North America. ParkMobile is available in over 700 cities.

battlecards.overview: A 2,100-person unified physical security platform company whose AutoVu ALPR module is a direct, well-proven competitor for US municipal parking enforcement. Sold only through certified channel partners.
battlecards.tldr: We win when the city wants detection across cameras it already owns and more than enforcement out of the patrol. We lose when the buyer is a security department standardising on one platform, or when they want a vendor with 42,500 clients behind the signature.
battlecards.quick_dismiss: Genetec is a serious product and the strongest competitor in this set. The distinction is scope: AutoVu is ALPR on their cameras, inside a security platform. We are a city intelligence layer on cameras the city already has, which also returns road and asset condition from the same drive. Ask what the patrol should deliver in three years.

where_we_win.headline: Their cameras versus the city's cameras
where_we_win.detail: AutoVu captures plates with Genetec SharpX cameras fitted to enforcement vehicles, so coverage is bounded by how many vehicles you equip. SenDISA runs on the camera estate and VMS the city already owns, with no infrastructure overhaul, so coverage scales without buying more hardware.

where_we_win.headline: One patrol pass, four departments
where_we_win.detail: The same drive returns 40-plus road defect types with severity ratings, a versioned asset and signage register, and worksite safety detection. Genetec publishes no road-condition or asset-register capability, so that is a second system and a second contract.

where_we_win.headline: The integration model is proven, not theoretical
where_we_win.detail: SenForce already powers gtechna's Ticket-by-Mail: our cameras capture the violation, an automated workflow builds the ticket and evidence package, and the notice is mailed after officer approval. It runs live in Pittsburgh, Kitchener and Medford. A city keeping its existing citation system is how most of our North American base is deployed.

where_we_win.headline: Buy direct, and see the price
where_we_win.detail: Genetec sells only through certified channel partners, so the city never gets a price from the vendor and the implementation relationship sits with a reseller whose capability varies by region. We contract directly.

where_we_win.headline: Calgary retendered globally and chose us again
where_we_win.detail: A customer since 2016, Calgary ran a full RFP in 2024 to replace its vehicle monitoring and enforcement technology and reselected SenSen: A$4.6M over five years with two further two-year options. That is an incumbent surviving open competition on exactly the replacement decision this prospect is making.

where_we_lose.headline: Scale and institutional safety
where_we_lose.detail: 42,500 clients in 159 countries, 2,100-plus staff and nearly 30 years of trading. Against that, our market capitalisation is around A$25M. In a risk-averse US procurement that asymmetry is the single hardest objection we face.
where_we_lose.counter: Do not fight it on size. Move to the specific decision: who has replaced an incumbent enforcement system in a comparable city recently, and what did the patrol return beyond citations.

where_we_lose.headline: Published payback, not just outcomes
where_we_lose.detail: Fort Lauderdale booted over 600 scofflaw vehicles and collected over $200,000 in unpaid fines in eight months, a 1400% rise in scofflaw identification, and recouped the system cost in about two months. That is a cleaner commercial story than we publish.
where_we_lose.counter: Match it with operational outcomes we can evidence, and offer a reference call rather than a case study.

where_we_lose.headline: One platform for security and parking
where_we_lose.detail: If the buyer also owns video surveillance, access control and intrusion, Security Center unifies all of it with one operator training burden. Parking alone rarely wins that argument.
where_we_lose.counter: Qualify early: if the economic buyer is the security department rather than parking or transport, this is their deal to lose. Partner rather than fight.

where_we_lose.headline: Professional services and certification depth
where_we_lose.detail: Remote and on-site professional services, a channel partner programme, a technology partner programme and an A&E consultant programme. We publish none of that.
where_we_lose.counter: Lead with direct access to the people who build the product, which a channel model cannot offer.

where_we_lose.headline: US grant funding support
where_we_lose.detail: Genetec runs a US-only Grants Support Team that helps public agencies navigate grant funding at no cost.
where_we_lose.counter: We offer grants coordination assistance and multi-year payment plans; make sure procurement knows it exists.

landmines.question: How many enforcement vehicles would we need to equip to cover the whole curb, and what does each additional vehicle cost?
landmines.why: AutoVu coverage scales with equipped vehicles because detection runs on its own SharpX cameras. It converts a per-unit hardware decision into a visible number.

landmines.question: Who holds the implementation contract - Genetec, or the reseller? And what happens if we change reseller mid-term?
landmines.why: Genetec serves customers exclusively through certified channel partners, so continuity of delivery sits with a third party.

landmines.question: Can the same patrol tell us which signs are faded and which roads are failing, or is that a separate procurement?
landmines.why: No published road-condition or asset-register capability. It reframes the comparison from enforcement to what the drive returns.

landmines.question: If we are not standardising on one security platform, what are we paying for in Security Center that parking will never use?
landmines.why: AutoVu sits inside a unified security platform. A parking-only buyer should test how much of that estate they actually need.

landmines.question: What is the published deployment timeframe, and who commits to it contractually?
landmines.why: Genetec publishes no deployment timeframe; projects are scoped by the partner. We publish 2-4 weeks for vision and 6-8 weeks for asset management.

objections.objection: Genetec is a far bigger, safer company than you.
objections.response: True, and if the decision is vendor size it is theirs. The decision we would put in front of you is coverage and scope: their ALPR runs on cameras you buy and fit to vehicles, ours runs on cameras you already own and also returns road and asset condition from the same drive. Calgary tested that at open retender in 2024 and renewed with us for up to nine years.

objections.objection: We already run Genetec Security Center for video and access control.
objections.response: Then keep it. We are a detection and intelligence layer, not a security platform, and we integrate through open REST APIs and webhooks into what you already run. The question is whether AutoVu covers the whole curb or only the vehicles you equip.

objections.objection: Fort Lauderdale paid for its AutoVu system in two months. Can you show that?
objections.response: That is a strong number and worth respecting. Ours is a different shape: no upfront capital expenditure at all, an annual subscription, and value that compounds because the same patrol feeds parking, road condition and asset data. Ask them what the payback looks like once you add a second system for asset surveys.

objections.objection: Our reseller has looked after us for years.
objections.response: Keep that relationship where it adds value. Worth asking what happens contractually if the reseller changes, and whether you can get a roadmap commitment from the vendor directly rather than through a partner.

pricing_comparison.text: Neither vendor publishes a price list, but the models differ. Genetec is channel-only, so a city gets a reseller quote covering SharpX cameras, in-vehicle hardware and Security Center licensing; its published commercial proof is payback, with Fort Lauderdale recouping its investment in about two months. SenSen is an annual subscription with no upfront capital expenditure and multi-year payment plans, and disclosed contract values imply roughly A$1 per head of population per year in large cities - Calgary at A$1.9M in year one and A$4.6M over five.

proof_quotes.quote: Within the first eight months of installing its first AutoVu ALPR system, the City of Fort Lauderdale was able to boot over 600 scofflaw vehicles and collect over $200,000 in unpaid fines.
Headquartered in Montreal, Canada, Genetec serves its customers via an extensive network of certified channel partners and consultants in over 159 countries.
Works with your existing cameras and VMS systems with zero downtime during deployment. No infrastructure overhaul required.

battlecards.overview: EasyPark Group, renamed Arrive in June 2025. The parent of ParkMobile, EasyPark, Flowbird, RingGo and Parkopedia: the demand and payments side of parking across 90-plus countries, with no published enforcement detection product.
battlecards.tldr: Mostly not a competitor. Arrive owns the driver payment relationship; we detect and evidence violations. We only collide where a city bundles payments and enforcement into one procurement, and we lose that on breadth of payments, not on detection.
battlecards.quick_dismiss: Arrive is the payments and demand layer, not the enforcement layer. ParkMobile is in 700-plus US cities and that is real reach, but there is no published violation-detection or mobile ALPR product. In most deals the right answer is that they complement us rather than replace us.

where_we_win.headline: They do not detect violations at all
where_we_win.detail: Arrive's published portfolio is payments, reservations, pay stations, mobility data and in-car navigation. There is no violation-detection or mobile ALPR enforcement product. If the requirement is enforcement, this is not a head-to-head comparison.

where_we_win.headline: Enforcement-grade evidence, built for challenge
where_we_win.detail: SenDISA produces court-grade evidence packages with officer review on every event. A payments platform knows who paid; it does not evidence who did not.

where_we_win.headline: More than parking from the same patrol
where_we_win.detail: Road defect detection, asset and signage registers and worksite safety come from the drive you already run. Arrive's data products are demand and traffic analysis, not street condition.

where_we_win.headline: Three integrations still bedding in
where_we_win.detail: Flowbird closed January 2025, Parkopedia February 2025, and the group rebranded in June 2025. That is three major changes inside eighteen months for a city signing a multi-year contract.

where_we_lose.headline: Payment reach we cannot match
where_we_lose.detail: ParkMobile is in over 700 US cities; the group spans 90-plus countries and 20,000 cities, and owns EasyPark, RingGo, Flowbird and Yellowbrick outright rather than integrating them.
where_we_lose.counter: Concede it immediately and position as complementary: they take payment, we detect non-payment. The two decisions are separable.

where_we_lose.headline: Incumbency through the payment app
where_we_lose.detail: If the city already runs ParkMobile, Arrive holds the driver relationship and the transaction data, which is a strong platform from which to extend.
where_we_lose.counter: Ask what their enforcement roadmap actually is, and on what evidence standard, before the city assumes the incumbent can cover it.

where_we_lose.headline: Pay station and kerbside estate
where_we_lose.detail: Flowbird supplies pay-and-display machines, park-and-charge and smart ticketing in over 6,000 cities across 80 countries. That is physical presence on the kerb we do not have.
where_we_lose.counter: Position as the layer above the hardware: we read the street regardless of whose meter is on it.

where_we_lose.headline: In-car distribution
where_we_lose.detail: Parkopedia puts parking and charging data, in-car payments and indoor navigation into automaker dashboards. That is a channel to the driver we have no equivalent for.
where_we_lose.counter: Not our market. Keep the conversation on the enforcement and asset decision.

landmines.question: Does the proposal include violation detection, or only payment and reservation?
landmines.why: Arrive publishes no enforcement detection product. The question separates the two scopes before they are bundled in evaluation.

landmines.question: If enforcement is in scope, whose detection technology is being proposed and what is the evidence standard when a citation is challenged?
landmines.why: A payments platform would need a detection partner. The city should know who that is and who carries the evidence standard.

landmines.question: Which Arrive are we contracting with? Flash still operates ParkWhiz and BestParking under the former Arrive Mobility name.
landmines.why: EasyPark bought the Arrive name from Flash in 2025. Two different US parking companies have used it, and procurement records can confuse them.

landmines.question: Flowbird, Parkopedia and the rebrand all landed within eighteen months. What has been committed on roadmap and support continuity?
landmines.why: Integration load is a delivery risk on a multi-year municipal contract.

objections.objection: We already use ParkMobile. Can't they just add enforcement?
objections.response: They may well partner for it, and that is worth asking directly: whose detection, and what evidence standard when a citation is contested. Keep ParkMobile for payments - we integrate with payment systems rather than replace them, and we detect the vehicles that never paid.

objections.objection: Arrive is in 90 countries and 20,000 cities. You are much smaller.
objections.response: On payments, yes, and we would not try to compete there. On enforcement detection they publish no product at all. These are two different purchases, and bundling them usually means one of them is not really being evaluated.

objections.objection: One vendor for payments and enforcement is simpler for us.
objections.response: It is, if one vendor genuinely does both. Ask to see the enforcement detection product and a reference city where it issues evidenced citations. That is the test.

pricing_comparison.text: The two are priced on different models and rarely compared line for line. Arrive publishes consumer transaction pricing through its apps but no municipal contract pricing; Flowbird pay stations are a capital purchase. SenSen is an annual subscription with no upfront capital expenditure. Where a city bundles payments and enforcement into one tender, insist the enforcement scope is priced separately so the detection capability is actually evaluated.

proof_quotes.quote: ParkMobile, LLC, is the leading provider of smart parking and mobility solutions in North America. ParkMobile is available in over 700 cities.
The consumer brands and mobile apps, such as EasyPark, RingGo, ParkMobile, and Flowbird, will remain unaffected for the foreseeable future.

notes.Which Arrive this is: Arrive here is EasyPark Group, renamed on 12 June 2025 and parent of ParkMobile, EasyPark, Flowbird, RingGo, Parkopedia, Yellowbrick and YourParkingSpace. It is not Arrive Mobility, the ParkWhiz and BestParking business that merged into Flash in January 2021; EasyPark bought the rights to the name from Flash. In the United States the group trades mainly as ParkMobile, in over 700 cities.
notes.They are not all competing for the same: Genetec is a direct competitor for municipal enforcement: AutoVu is mobile and fixed ALPR inside the Security Center platform. Arrive is the payments and demand layer and publishes no violation-detection product, so it is usually an integration partner rather than a rival. Treat a tender that bundles payments and enforcement as two decisions, or the detection capability will not be properly evaluated.
notes.Buyer reviews: Rating and Market voice are deliberately unscored. Genetec Security Center is reviewed on G2, Gartner Peer Insights and Capterra at roughly 4 out of 5, but SenSen.ai has no buyer-review presence at all and Arrive's public ratings are consumer app-store scores for ParkMobile and EasyPark, which say nothing about how a city buyer rates the product. Scoring a category where only one of three vendors is rated would distort the leader badge, so it is left empty and the Genetec review signal is carried as prose instead.
notes.Where the accuracy figures are not compa: SenSen publishes over 98% ALPR accuracy and 99% accurate evidence packages, and those are self-reported. Genetec publishes no comparable accuracy figure. This card therefore makes no accuracy comparison and asks instead for contested-citation overturn rates on comparable deployments.
notes.Hosting claims: SenSen's IRAP Protected assessment and Sydney and Melbourne Azure hosting apply to Australian deployments. For United States deployments the company states regional Azure hosting, so no IRAP or US-specific accreditation is claimed in this report.
notes.Research method: Exa neural search over primary sources, then direct reading of ASX filings, Genetec's corporate fact sheet and published case studies, Arrive and Flash announcements, and trade press. Vendor case studies are marked as vendor sources, not independent.
